title: Shunt heatsink is the PCB copper pour (no discrete heatsinks)
rule: Every shunt (RS* refs) must be surrounded by wide 2 oz copper pours on the high-current nets that cover its full pad area and extend to the nearest high-current connector pads; no discrete or finned heatsink is allowed anywhere on any module.
rationale: Section 6.6 states 'The shunt dissipates 0.2 to 1.5 W depending on rail and value. Its heatsink is the PCB copper: the same wide 2 oz pour that carries the current, plus thermal vias around the shunt pads.' Discrete heatsinks are explicitly prohibited.
scope: All RS* footprints on every module PCB. High-current nets identified by _HI/_LO suffix or '12V' in net name (same derivation as cec_synth_pipeline._net_currents).
check_method: Verify each RS* footprint has at least one ZONE on its net covering its courtyard bbox on F.Cu or B.Cu. Absence of filled zone on the high-current net at each RS* location = violation. (Cannot reliably verify zone fill headlessly; requires pcbnew zone inspection.)
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6: 'Its heatsink is the PCB copper: the same wide 2 oz pour that carries the current, plus thermal vias around the shunt pads.'

title: Thermal via array around every shunt pad
rule: Each shunt pad (RS* parts) must have a thermal-via array punching through to the inner GND plane(s). Via drill must be sized for current contribution (at minimum 0.5 mm drill / 0.9 mm pad per netclass). For EPS/PCIe per-cable shunts at 40-55 A design current, copper-filled vias, plated slots, or copper coin/inlay are required to avoid via fusing (verified by physics_gates 'via over-temp').
rationale: Section 6.7: 'Size each path's via array for full current. For 20A, copper-filled vias or a plated slot beat a large hollow-via field. For the ~40 to 55A EPS/PCIe per-cable class, a copper coin or inlay is the right tool and gives a vertical heat path to the chassis.' CLAUDE.md DONE note: 'Verified on the routed+poured EPS @40A/enclosed: ... vias flagged FUSING (the §6.7/OQ-10 vertical-transition concern) -- 3 real thermal gates.'
scope: All RS* footprints. EPS/PCIe shunts (0.5 mΩ, up to 55 A) are the most critical.
check_method: For each RS* footprint pad: count PCB_VIA_T items on the same net within the shunt's courtyard bbox extended by 2 mm. If count = 0 flag 'no thermal vias at shunt RS{n}'. physics_gates 'via over-temp' fires when IPC-2221 model shows via T > 105 C at the design current.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7: 'Size each path's via array for full current... a copper coin or inlay is the right tool and gives a vertical heat path to the chassis.'

title: Bare un-anodized TIM contact land under EPS/PCIe high-current shunts for chassis coupling
rule: EPS and PCIe module PCBs must include a bare, un-anodized copper contact land (B.Cu, no soldermask, no finish) beneath each per-cable shunt to accept a TIM (thermal interface material) pad for conduction to the anodized 6063 aluminium chassis. This land must align with the chassis mounting surface beneath each shunt location.
rationale: Section 6.6 (v3.8 design-review decision): 'Spec a TIM pad and a bare, un-anodized contact land under the high-current EPS/PCIe shunts, where the 0.8 to 1.5 W of dissipation makes the self-heating term dominant. The anodized 6063 is an insulating contact, the corner M3 screws are point contact, and no thermal interface is otherwise specified, so the path into the chassis raises shunt self-heating and erodes the low-TCR accuracy (the error term is TCR x deltaT).'
scope: RS* footprints on eps-8pin and pcie-8pin-* modules. (24-pin shunts up to 0.8 W noted as lower priority in §6.6.)
check_method: Verify B.Cu copper zone or pad exists beneath each RS* centroid with no soldermask layer assignment (no B.Mask coverage). Partial: can check for a dedicated B.Cu zone labelled as the shunt net in the RS* courtyard bbox. Exact TIM land geometry requires human or fab verification.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6: 'Spec a TIM pad and a bare, un-anodized contact land under the high-current EPS/PCIe shunts, where the 0.8 to 1.5 W of dissipation makes the self-heating term dominant.'

title: Conductor temperature rise must not exceed 30 C rise / 105 C absolute (IPC-2221 model)
rule: For any routed high-current net (nets with _HI/_LO suffix, 12V nets, GND return), the IPC-2221/2152 analytic temperature rise at design current must be <= 30 C dT and <= 105 C absolute, with ambient = 50 C for enclosed_passive / 35 C for airflow environments.
rationale: cec_synth_pipeline.physics_gates: dT_max=30 C, T_max=105 C as pipeline gates. CLAUDE.md: 'cable pours dT 18-46C (hottest the thinnest pour, T=96C)... correctly WITHHELD release (residual DFM + conductor-over-temp + fusing-via flags)'. Section 6.3 current targets drive the sizing input.
scope: All *_HI, *_LO, *12V*, GND nets on high-current module boards (eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-standard). Ambient parametrized by thermal_env (cfg.params).
check_method: Run cec_synth_pipeline.electrothermal_solve() on the routed board; physics_gates() fires 'conductor over-temp' flags. Check method is the existing THERMAL armed analysis.
source: scripts/cec_synth_pipeline.py: 'dt_max = cfg.params.get("dT_max_C", 30.0)' and 'T_max_C: 105.0'; CLAUDE.md done entry: 'cable pours dT 18-46C... conductor-over-temp... correctly WITHHELD release'

title: Shunt self-heating must not exceed temperature budget at design current
rule: Each shunt (RS* refs) I^2*R dissipation must result in a junction temperature <= 105 C (using shunt_rth_CW=25 C/W for a 2512 part+pad) at the worst-case per-cable current from §6.3. For EPS/PCIe at 55 A sustained per cable: P = 55^2 * 0.5e-3 = 1.51 W -> dT = 1.51 * 25 = 37.8 C, so ambient ceiling for EPS/PCIe is 105 - 38 = 67 C; with TIM and chassis coupling this budget is restored.
rationale: Section 6.6: 'The shunt dissipates 0.2 to 1.5 W depending on rail and value.' cec_synth_pipeline.physics_gates fires 'shunt over-temp' when shunt T > T_max (105 C default). Section 6.4 worst case EPS/PCIe = 1.5 W at 55 A per cable.
scope: RS* refs on all module boards. Worst case is EPS/PCIe 0.5 mΩ at 55 A (1.51 W). 24-pin main rails 2 mΩ at 20 A = 0.8 W. 12VHPWR per-pin 1 mΩ at 9.5-12 A = 0.09-0.14 W per pin.
check_method: electrothermal_solve() shunts list: P = I^2 * R_ohm, dT = P * shunt_rth_CW, T = ambient + dT. physics_gates 'shunt over-temp' already fires on T > 105.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: 'EPS, per cable | 0.5 mΩ | 27 mV / 1.5 W at 55A'; §6.6: 'The shunt dissipates 0.2 to 1.5 W depending on rail and value.'

title: TH1 (shunt/board-temp NTC) placed adjacent to the shunt row / high-current connector
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, TH1 must be placed within the shunt row zone — physically near the J3 input connector's +12V pins / the inline shunts — to measure board/shunt temperature and the mated 12VHPWR connector heat. TH1 centroid must be within 5 mm of the nearest RS* shunt centroid.
rationale: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient'; '— TH1 at the J3 +12V pins, TH2 ambient'. Section 6.1: 'One NTC sits at the J3 input connector's +12V pins (the on-board mated pair, and the actual melt site)'. The NTC's purpose is to detect contact-resistance heating = the 12VHPWR failure mode.
scope: TH1 ref on modules/12vhpwr-standard (identified by Value containing 'NTC' or footprint containing 'NTC_0402' and Reference 'TH1'). RS* shunts on the same board.
check_method: Compute distance from TH1 centroid (from PCB footprint positions) to nearest RS* centroid. If > 5 mm, flag violation. Also check TH1 is on the same side (F.Cu) as the shunts.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.7 note: 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient'; '— TH1 at the J3 +12V pins'; CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1: 'One NTC sits at the J3 input connector's +12V pins (the on-board mated pair, and the actual melt site)'

title: TH2 (ambient reference NTC) placed at a thermally uncoupled board location away from heat sources
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, TH2 must be placed at a cool board location — away from the shunt row, the high-current connector (J3/J4), and the LDO (U3/LP5907) — to measure ambient board temperature. TH2 centroid must be at least 10 mm from any RS* shunt centroid and at least 5 mm from any LDO (LP5907*) or ESP32 footprint centroid.
rationale: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient'. The dT = TH1 - TH2 is the primary connector-overheat alarm; if TH2 is heated by nearby dissipators the alarm threshold shifts up and melt events go undetected. Section 6.1: 'one is an ambient reference at a cool board edge.'
scope: TH2 ref on modules/12vhpwr-standard. RS*, LP5907*, and ESP32 refs are the thermal exclusion zone.
check_method: Compute distance from TH2 centroid to nearest RS* centroid (must be >= 10 mm) and to nearest LDO centroid (must be >= 5 mm). If either fails, flag violation.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'TH2 ambient'; CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1: 'one is an ambient reference at a cool board edge'

title: Hub Standard TH1 (board-temp NTC) placed away from LDO and power dissipators
rule: On the Hub Standard, TH1 (board temperature NTC on TEMP_HUB net -> ADC1 IO3) must be placed away from the LP5907 LDO (U4), the TPS2121 power mux (U5/U7), the SK6812 LED chain, and the 4700 µF hold-up capacitor, to give a representative board ambient. TH1 centroid must be >= 5 mm from the LP5907 or TPS2121 centroids.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'ADDED a board-temp sensor to Hub Standard: TH1 (this NTC) high-side from +3V3, R25 10k -> TEMP_HUB -> ADC1 IO3'. The measurement is only useful as an ambient if it is not dominated by LDO or mux self-heating.
scope: TH1 ref on hubs/hub-standard (Value 'NTC 10k', net TEMP_HUB). LP5907*, TPS2121* refs are the exclusion sources.
check_method: Compute distance from TH1 centroid to LP5907 and TPS2121 centroids. If < 5 mm flag advisory.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'ADDED a board-temp sensor to Hub Standard: TH1 (this NTC)... PCB place/route pending GUI'

title: Sense ICs (INA238/INA228/INA240) thermally separated from shunt self-heating zone
rule: Sense ICs (INA238*, INA228*, INA240* refs) must be placed adjacent to the shunt's Kelvin sense edge (inner edge, per §6.8) but positioned so the IC body is NOT directly above or below the shunt's power dissipation zone; the IC body should be beside (not on top of) the shunt in the direction of the sense tap, minimizing thermal coupling of shunt heat into the IC die.
rationale: CLAUDE.md action item -2 considerations list: 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)' and 'thermal separation'. Section 6.8: 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor.' The INA238/INA228 have no internal temperature correction, so shunt-radiated heat skews the gain; adjacent means beside the inner edge, not stacked above the hot body.
scope: INA238*, INA228*, INA240* refs adjacent to RS* refs. Pairing derived: each sense IC owns the RS* shunt whose _HI/_LO nets it reads (same derivation as cec_score.Rules.from_board Kelvin pairs).
check_method: For each (INA*, RS*) Kelvin pair: compute centroid-to-centroid distance (must be <= 6 mm for Kelvin wire length), AND verify the INA centroid is NOT within the RS* courtyard bbox extended by 1 mm (i.e. beside, not on top). Failure: distance > 6 mm (not adjacent) or INA inside shunt footprint bbox (stacked).
existing_checker: cec_score.py (kelvin_ok gate verifies connectivity; does not verify physical proximity)
source: CLAUDE.md action -2: 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'; CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8: 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor.'

title: LP5907 LDO thermally separated from NTC thermistors
rule: The LP5907MFX LDO regulator (U3 on modules, U4 on Hub Standard) must be separated from any NTC thermistor (TH1, TH2) by at least 5 mm to prevent LDO self-heating (~0.15 W estimated) from biasing the temperature reading.
rationale: Derived from cec_synth_pipeline._part_power_w which assigns 0.15 W to LDO parts, and the thermal_separated strategy which nudges hot parts away from NTCs. NTC accuracy requires it read an unperturbed temperature; LP5907 at 250 mA load can raise its case >10 C above ambient.
scope: All LP5907* refs (U3 on modules, U4 on Hub) vs TH1, TH2 refs on the same board.
check_method: Compute Euclidean distance between LP5907 centroid and each TH* centroid. Flag if < 5 mm.
source: scripts/cec_synth_pipeline.py _part_power_w: 'if ref.startswith("U") and ("LP59" in v ... ): return 0.15' (LDO/regulator power class); CLAUDE.md action -2: 'thermal sep ... as hard constraints/score terms'

title: ESP32 module separated from high-current shunt thermal zone
rule: The ESP32 module (U1, any ESP32-* footprint) must be placed in the control/logic zone, separated from the shunt row and high-current connector pair (J_IN/J_OUT) by the logic partition of the board. Minimum separation from any RS* shunt centroid: 10 mm for 12VHPWR (per-pin shunts, 0.14 W each but 6 total = 0.85 W aggregate), 15 mm for EPS/PCIe (per-cable 1.5 W).
rationale: CLAUDE.md action -2: 'thermal separation' as a deferred hard constraint. Section 6.6: 'The anodized 6063 aluminum production chassis is the heat spreader. Couple the high-current copper to the chassis through the mounting points' -- the sense electronics (ESP32) should be in the cool section. ESP32 ADC accuracy degrades with die temperature; the S3-MINI-1 and C6-MINI-1 have no internal temperature-reference correction.
scope: U1 (ESP32 module) vs RS* refs on every module board.
check_method: Compute distance from U1 centroid to nearest RS* centroid. Flag if < 10 mm (12VHPWR) or < 15 mm (EPS/PCIe). Board type determined from directory name or board_id in cfg.
source: CLAUDE.md action -2 considerations: 'thermal sep ... as hard constraints/score terms'; CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6 layout guidance

title: REF3030 voltage reference thermally isolated from shunts and LDO
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, U4 (REF3030) must be placed in the cool logic zone, separated from the nearest RS* shunt by at least 8 mm and from the LP5907 LDO by at least 4 mm. The REF3030 temperature coefficient (Typ 5 ppm/°C) means a 10 C temperature rise adds 50 ppm = 0.005% error; at 30 C rise from a nearby shunt this is 0.015%, partially negating the ratiometric improvement.
rationale: CLAUDE.md v3.10: 'The reference's *stability* (not just accuracy) is what lets the module trend the delivery-path source impedance (dV/dI) and absolute droop as a connector-degradation early-warning, instead of mistaking ADC drift for it.' A thermally coupled REF3030 tracks shunt current (via Joule heating) and introduces a current-correlated reference error that firmware cannot distinguish from true droop.
scope: U4 (REF3030) on modules/12vhpwr-standard. RS* and LP5907* are the thermal exclusion sources.
check_method: Compute distance from REF3030 (U4) centroid to nearest RS* centroid (must be >= 8 mm) and to LP5907 centroid (must be >= 4 mm). BOM field Value = 'REF3030' identifies the part.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.10: 'The reference's stability (not just accuracy) is what lets the module trend... instead of mistaking ADC drift for it.' CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1 REF3030 note

title: High-current rails routed as copper pours on outer layers (F.Cu/B.Cu), not thin inner traces
rule: All high-current nets (*_HI, *_LO, 12V nets carrying > 5 A) must be routed as copper POURS on F.Cu and/or B.Cu (outer layers) in 2 oz copper, not as single thin traces on inner layers. An inner-layer trace carrying a cable current (40-55 A EPS/PCIe) with only the via-array cross-section as the thermal path will over-temperature. Inner layers (L2/L3) are for GND plane and power rail distribution at module-level currents only.
rationale: Section 6.7: 'Run inner copper at 2 oz on both the L3 rails and the L2 return. Alternative to evaluate per module: keep the high-current rails and shunts on L1 in 2 oz so current never leaves the top layer, trading a busier top layer for far fewer high-current vias and an intact ground plane.' CLAUDE.md DONE: 'GND (already a plane), the 12V SENSEC nets, and the power rails belong as FILLED POURS; FR routes only signal/control'. Verified EPS physics: 'cable pours dT 18-46C (hottest the thinnest pour, T=96C)'.
scope: SENSEC*_HI, SENSEC*_LO, and any net carrying > 5 A (from _net_currents model) on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-standard.
check_method: For each high-current net (I > 5 A per _net_currents): check for at least one ZONE on F.Cu or B.Cu with GetNetname() == net. If the net has only PCB_TRACE_T items and no ZONE items flagging it as a pour, fire 'high-current net not poured: {net}'.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline.electrothermal_solve (poured set; conductor-over-temp indirectly catches underpoured nets)
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7: 'keep the high-current rails and shunts on L1 in 2 oz so current never leaves the top layer'; CLAUDE.md: 'current is carried by copper AREA... the power rails belong as FILLED POURS'

title: Ambient temperature for thermal analysis set to 50 C (enclosed passive) not 25 C bench
rule: All electrothermal analysis and derating calculations must use ambient = 50 C for enclosed_passive (normal PC case, no forced airflow), or 35 C for bench/airflow. The default must be enclosed_passive = 50 C; the board must pass the conductor/via/shunt temperature gates at 50 C ambient, not at 25 C.
rationale: cec_synth_pipeline: '_AMBIENT = {"enclosed_passive": 50.0, "airflow": 35.0, "worst_case": 60.0}'. CLAUDE.md Stage-1: 'Collected the EPS answers live (wired-only, hand-off, enclosed/passive)'. The modules are inside a PC chassis without direct airflow; using 25 C ambient underestimates conductor temperature by 25 C, changing the fusing-via margin from pass to fail.
scope: All high-current module boards. Applies to every electrothermal_solve() call.
check_method: Verify cfg.params['thermal_env'] is not overridden to 'airflow' without explicit user instruction. Check that the THERMAL gate run uses ambient >= 50 C (enclosed_passive). Deterministically testable via cfg inspection.
source: scripts/cec_synth_pipeline.py: '_AMBIENT = {"enclosed_passive": 50.0, "airflow": 35.0, "worst_case": 60.0}'; CLAUDE.md Stage-1 answers: 'enclosed/passive'

title: Per-cable shunts distributed (not clustered) to spread thermal load across the board
rule: On EPS and PCIe modules with multiple cables, the per-cable shunts (RS1, RS2 on EPS; RS1-RS3 on PCIe) must be spread along the cable dimension (top-to-bottom or left-to-right) rather than clustered, so their thermal zones do not additively overheat a single board region. Minimum inter-shunt pitch should equal or exceed the connector pin pitch (approximately 4.2 mm per column), which is guaranteed by the interposer geometry when each cable's IN/OUT connector pair is a separate physical connector.
rationale: Section 6.6: 'Per-cable sensing spreads heat across the module's two or three cable shunts rather than concentrating it. Each per-cable shunt and its coin or via field is a hotspot, so the copper-pour, thermal-via, and chassis-coupling treatment applies at each one.' The spreading is inherent to the interposer architecture but must be verified in the PCB layout.
scope: RS1..RS3 on eps-8pin and pcie-8pin-* modules.
check_method: Verify that no two RS* centroids are within 5 mm of each other (they should be separated by at least one cable-column pitch). Derive shunt refs by footprint pattern match to 2512 land + Value matching mΩ-range.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6: 'Per-cable sensing spreads heat across the module's two or three cable shunts rather than concentrating it. Each per-cable shunt and its coin or via field is a hotspot...'

title: Continuous GND plane beneath sense ICs and NTCs (signal return, thermal reference)
rule: The L2 inner GND pour must be continuous and uninterrupted under the sense ICs (INA238*, INA228*, INA240*, INA181*) and under the NTC thermistors (TH1, TH2), with no large anti-pad voids from high-current via arrays intruding into this area. Anti-pad voids from the high-current cable region (the shunt via arrays) must not extend within 3 mm of any INA* or TH* centroid.
rationale: Section 6.7: 'Via arrays punch anti-pad voids in the L2 ground pour; keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids.' A fragmented GND plane under the sense ICs creates a return-path discontinuity and a thermal step that biases the NTC reading if the GND plane is the thermal coupling path from chassis.
scope: INA*, TH* refs vs RS* shunt via arrays on all module boards.
check_method: Approximate: for each INA* or TH* centroid, check that no RS* centroid is within 5 mm in the same column (shunt via arrays radiate outward). Full check requires zone fill analysis (partial). Flag if INA* or TH* centroid is within 4 mm of an RS* centroid (via-void halo approximated as 4 mm radius).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7: 'Via arrays punch anti-pad voids in the L2 ground pour; keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids.'

title: Outer layers (F.Cu, B.Cu) must be 2 oz copper on high-current module boards
rule: EPS, PCIe, and 12VHPWR Standard module PCBs must be specified as 2 oz copper on F.Cu and B.Cu outer layers. This doubles the thermal conductance of the copper pour and directly halves the dT from the IPC-2221 model for a given cross-section. Inner layers also 2 oz per §6.7 guidance.
rationale: Section 6.7: 'Run inner copper at 2 oz on both the L3 rails and the L2 return.' The 12VHPWR routing plan documented in CLAUDE.md: '12V lane 2.5mm on F.Cu + 2.5mm mirrored on B.Cu paralleled (~13A @ <10C, IPC-2221 2oz)'. The electrothermal model in cec_synth_pipeline uses CU_OZ_MM = 0.0348 mm/oz * oz_count -- if stackup is declared 1 oz, the dT doubles.
scope: All high-current module boards: eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro. Verified via the stackup declaration in the .kicad_pcb (board setup -> physical stackup).
check_method: Parse the .kicad_pcb stackup section: verify F.Cu and B.Cu layers have thickness >= 0.07 mm (= 2 oz = 0.0696 mm). 1 oz = 0.0348 mm. KiCad stores this in (layer ... (thickness ...)) under (setup (stackup ...)).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7: 'Run inner copper at 2 oz on both the L3 rails and the L2 return.' CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR routing plan: '2oz outer / 1oz inner (hpwr: 12V on both outers, GND both inners)'

title: High-current pour corridor J_IN -> shunt -> J_OUT kept clear of sense and control components
rule: The high-current copper corridor (the rectangular band between J_IN and J_OUT connectors passing through the shunts) must be free of sense ICs, MCU, LDO, CAN transceiver, and NTC thermistors. Only shunts (RS*), their decoupling caps (CF*), and INA input filter resistors (RFH*, RFL*) are permitted within the corridor. The corridor width equals the connector row width (~column pitch * number of 12V pins).
rationale: CLAUDE.md action -2: 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as a deferred hard constraint that the auto-placer lacks. Placing logic inside the high-current corridor physically conflicts with the pour fill (large copper blocks the routing channel for sense lines) and thermally stresses components with high-J copper.
scope: J_IN* / J_OUT* connector pairs on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-standard. Corridor = bounding box between J_IN and J_OUT in the current-flow axis (y-axis for top-in/bottom-out layout), width = connector column span.
check_method: Define corridor as xmin/xmax of J_IN or J_OUT pad extents x ymin(J_IN pads) to ymax(J_OUT pads). Check no ESP32, INA*, LP5907*, TJA*, TH* centroid falls within the corridor bbox. Connectors and RS* shunts are exempt.
source: CLAUDE.md action -2: 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as a required hard constraint; §6.7 layout guidance

title: 4700 µF aluminium electrolytic hold-up cap (C1, Hub Standard) derated for operating temperature
rule: C1 (4700 µF / 16 V aluminium electrolytic, Panasonic EEVFK1C472M) on Hub Standard must not be placed adjacent to the LP5907 LDO (U4) or TPS2121 mux (U5/U7). The aluminium electrolytic has a rated temperature limit; high ambient accelerates electrolyte evaporation. Minimum separation from LP5907 and TPS2121: 5 mm.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'LP5907 LDO, 4700 uF aluminum electrolytic hold-up — Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16 V, corrected from polymer v1.9'. Aluminium electrolytics are lifetime-limited by temperature (Arrhenius: each 10 C above rated halves life). The LDO and mux are the primary thermal sources on the Hub.
scope: C1 ref on hubs/hub-standard (identified by Value '4700uF' or '4700u' and part Panasonic EEVFK1C472M). LP5907 (U4) and TPS2121 (U5, U7) are the exclusion sources.
check_method: Compute distance from C1 centroid to U4 and U5/U7 centroids. Flag advisory if < 5 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'LP5907 LDO, 4700 uF aluminum electrolytic hold-up — Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16V'; thermal derating standard practice for aluminium electrolytic capacitors

title: Shunt power dissipation must be within rated power with margin (design sustained vs rating)
rule: Each shunt must dissipate no more than 60% of its rated power at design sustained current (not transient). For EPS/PCIe 0.5 mΩ at 55 A: 1.51 W at sustained; shunt rated at 3 W (CSS2H candidate) -> 50% of rating, acceptable. For 24-pin 2 mΩ at 20 A: 0.8 W against a 5 W (3 W conservative) rating -> 27% (16%). Verify BOM shunt power rating >= 1.67x the I^2*R at design sustained current.
rationale: Section 6.4: 'power rating well above the dissipation above... at 0.8 W the part runs near 16% of its 5 W rating (27% even on the 3 W figure), so self-heating rise is far lower for the same dissipation.' The 60% ceiling (1.67x margin) is the conservative industry rule for sustained operation at elevated ambient.
scope: All RS* parts on every module. BOM field 'Power' or part datasheet rating. Design current from §6.3 table.
check_method: Read Value (resistance in mΩ) and BOM 'Power' field (rated W) for each RS*. Compute P_design = I_design^2 * R_ohm (I_design from _net_currents model for that board). Check P_design / P_rated < 0.6. Flag BOM if BOM Power field absent (cannot check).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: 'the part runs near 16% of its 5 W rating (27% even on the 3 W figure), so self-heating rise is far lower for the same dissipation'

title: 12VHPWR Standard module must populate both TH1 and TH2 NTC thermistors
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module BOM and schematic must include exactly two NTC thermistors: TH1 (shunt/board temp, TEMP1 net -> ADC2 IO13) and TH2 (ambient, TEMP2 net -> ADC2 IO14), both Murata NCP15XH103F03RC (LCSC C77131), footprint cec-Resistor_SMD:NTC_0402_1005Metric. Absence of either violates the thermal monitoring requirement and removes the dT connector-overheat alarm.
rationale: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'the 12VHPWR Standard module gains two NTC thermistor dividers... TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient. INA240 has no die-temp sensor (unlike the 24-pin INA228), so this is the module's only temperature source + the Appendix C.2 datum.' The 12VHPWR failure mode is contact-resistance melt detected by temperature rise.
scope: modules/12vhpwr-standard BOM and schematic. TH1 on net TEMP1, TH2 on net TEMP2.
check_method: Check BOM for refs TH1 and TH2 both present with Value 'NTC 10k' and MPN 'NCP15XH103F03RC'. Check netlist for TEMP1 and TEMP2 net nodes containing TH1 and TH2 respectively. Missing either = hard violation.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'the 12VHPWR Standard module gains two NTC thermistor dividers (real part Murata NCP15XH103F03RC / C77131; TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient)'

title: Hub Standard must populate TH1 board-temp NTC
rule: Hub Standard BOM and schematic must include TH1 (Murata NCP15XH103F03RC, LCSC C77131) on net TEMP_HUB -> ADC1 IO3, with series resistor R25 10k (C25744) and filter cap C16 100 nF (C1525). Absence violates the board-health monitoring requirement.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'ADDED a board-temp sensor to Hub Standard: TH1 (this NTC) high-side from +3V3, R25 10k (C25744) to GND, C16 100nF (C1525) node filter -> TEMP_HUB -> ADC1 IO3'.
scope: hubs/hub-standard BOM and schematic.
check_method: Check BOM for TH1 ref with Value 'NTC 10k'. Check netlist for net TEMP_HUB containing TH1, R25, and a GPIO node. Missing TH1 = violation.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'ADDED a board-temp sensor to Hub Standard: TH1 (this NTC) high-side from +3V3, R25 10k to GND, C16 100nF node filter -> TEMP_HUB -> ADC1 IO3'

title: 12VHPWR Standard INA240 has no die-temperature sensor — NTC thermistors are the ONLY thermal source
rule: Firmware and any test coverage for the 12VHPWR Standard must NOT attempt to read die temperature from the INA240A3 parts (they lack it, unlike INA228). All thermal data on this module comes exclusively from TH1/TH2 NTCs. Any schematic annotation or BOM note implying an INA240 internal temperature register is incorrect and must be flagged.
rationale: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'the INA240 has no die-temp sensor (unlike the 24-pin INA228), so this is the module's only temperature source + the Appendix C.2 datum.' This is a documented distinction that can lead to firmware errors if overlooked.
scope: modules/12vhpwr-standard schematic symbols and BOM. INA240A3 refs U10-U15.
check_method: Check that no INA240 symbol has a 'Temperature' or 'Die_Temp' property set in the schematic. Partially checkable via BOM field inspection. Flag if any INA240 symbol in the schematic has a temperature pin connected to a net other than GND or NC.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'the INA240 has no die-temp sensor (unlike the 24-pin INA228), so this is the module's only temperature source'

title: High-current connectors (J_IN, J_OUT, J3, J4) counted as thermal sources for adjacent component placement
rule: Connectors carrying > 10 A continuous (J_IN, J_OUT on EPS/PCIe; J3, J4 on 12VHPWR) must be treated as thermal sources in placement. No temperature-sensitive component (NTC, REF3030, precision divider R5/R6) should be placed within 5 mm of these connector bodies.
rationale: Section 6.1 (12VHPWR connector temperature note): 'One NTC sits at the J3 input connector's +12V pins (the on-board mated pair, and the actual melt site)' — TH1 is deliberately close to J3 to sense its heat, but precision components must be shielded from it. RJ-45 contact resistance at 1.5 A/pin is < 1 mW/contact and is not a concern; it is only the high-current PSU connectors (EPS/PCIe Mini-Fit Jr, 12VHPWR 12V-2x6) that contribute significant heat.
scope: J* refs with role power_in/power_out on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-standard. Temperature-sensitive refs: TH2 (ambient), REF3030 (U4), precision divider R5/R6.
check_method: For each J* of type power_in/power_out: compute distance to TH2, REF3030 (U4), R5, R6 centroids. Flag advisory if < 5 mm (TH1 is the exception — it is intentionally adjacent to J3).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1: 'One NTC sits at the J3 input connector's +12V pins (the on-board mated pair, and the actual melt site)'; §6.6 chassis thermal coupling design note

title: Copper pours must be filled AFTER autorouting (not before) to avoid stranding Kelvin sense taps
rule: The workflow order must be: (1) route all signal and sense nets first (Freerouting or manual), (2) THEN add/fill power pours as additive same-net copper on the already-routed board. Filling pours before routing can cause the router to route the force net differently and leave the Kelvin sense tap stranded on an isolated pour island.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'The fix is to pour AFTER the route: FR routes everything first (sense connected, gates pass), THEN lay the 12V pours as ADDITIVE same-net copper — a pour on an already-routed net can only ADD copper, never strand the sense tap that shares the net node. Two attempts both regressed kelvin_ok [when poured before route].'
scope: All high-current module boards processed by cec_fr.add_power_pours() / import_ses(). Applies to the synthesis pipeline route_swarm stage.
check_method: Check that in the pipeline execution order, add_power_pours() is called after import_ses() (after the SES import of the routed board). In the decision log, verify pour step comes after route step. The kelvin_ok gate firing after a pour-then-route sequence is the symptom.
existing_checker: cec_score.py kelvin_ok gate (catches the symptom if violated)
source: CLAUDE.md DONE entry: 'The fix is to pour AFTER the route... a pour on an already-routed net can only ADD copper, never strand the sense tap... Two attempts both regressed kelvin_ok'
